chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever is poor, let him eat reasonably.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who manages something for the orphans and he is needy, having nothing to sustain him, so he collects their wealth and stands in their place, so let him eat in a measured manner and not be extravagant; and if it was that standing in their place does not pre-occupy him from what he works for himself, so he should not take anything from their wealth.'
ai.seo_question: How much can an orphan's custodian eat from the orphan's wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the conditions under which a custodian (wali) may consume from an orphan's wealth, distinguishing between a needy custodian who requires sustenance while managing the assets and one who does not. It establishes the principle of 'bil-ma'ruf' (in a reasonable manner), ensuring that consumption is proportional to the effort of management and not excessive, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness and preventing exploitation of vulnerable assets.
